issues.title: Proving who you are, again
issues.category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Every institution verifies you separately, none of them trust each other's verification, and each wants a different combination of documents you must locate, copy and produce in person.

details.description: A bank, a landlord, an employer, a phone company and a government office will each run their own identity check on the same person in the same month.
details.energy_note: Verified five times, trusted once each.

details.aspect: The document you need is with the thing you cannot do
details.description: Proof of address needs a utility bill; the utility needs an account; the account needs proof of address. The loop is broken by whoever bends first.
details.energy_note: A circle you have to talk your way out of.

details.aspect: Certified copies cost money and a trip
details.description: A notary, a solicitor or a post office charges per document and is open during the hours you are at work.

Two forms of ID, one of which must be dated within three months. His payslip is digital and 'not accepted', the tenancy agreement is in his partner's name, and the branch appointment is eleven days out.
details.energy_note: Employed, solvent, and unbanked for six weeks.

details.description: Every proof has a shelf life. The bundle you assembled in March is invalid in August, so the work is done again from scratch.
details.energy_note: A job you finish and then have to redo.

details.aspect: How this dataset relates to the other one
details.description: Everything here is imposed on anyone. The hurdles in assets/text/iran are imposed on top, by nationality and status. The immigration-specific costs are additive to these, not instead of them: an Iranian applicant proves identity to a bank AND to a visa officer, waits in a hospital queue AND in a security screening queue.
details.energy_note: The same day, plus a second one nobody else has.
details.notes: Deliberate design: the baseline makes the specific disadvantage measurable.

issues.title: The renewal treadmill
issues.category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Passport, licence, registration, insurance, membership, subscription, permit. Each has its own cycle and its own portal, so something is always about to lapse and the lapse is always your fault.

details.description: Nothing renews on the same date. The cognitive load is keeping a calendar of other people's deadlines.
details.energy_note: Twelve deadlines, none of which are about anything.

details.aspect: Lapsing is punished, renewing is not rewarded
details.description: Late fees, invalidated cover, penalty points. Doing it on time gets you exactly where you already were.
details.energy_note: The best available outcome is no change.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the licence in the drawer
details.description: It expired fourteen months ago. He notices at a car hire desk on the first morning of a holiday.

details.aspect: Auto-renew solves it by overcharging you
details.description: The way to never lapse is to let everything renew automatically, which is also how you pay the loyalty price on all of it.
details.energy_note: Convenience, sold back to you annually.

issues.title: Open when you are at work
issues.category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Offices, clinics, banks and tradespeople operate during working hours, so accessing them costs annual leave or lost pay.

details.description: The task takes twenty minutes. Getting to it takes half a day.

details.aspect: Waiting in for a delivery or a tradesperson
details.description: An eight-hour window means a whole day surrendered for a visit that lasts twenty minutes, and the visit is often rescheduled.
details.energy_note: A day spent waiting, then done again next week.

details.description: Twice he took the afternoon off. Twice nobody came. The third time he takes the whole day and they arrive at 16:50.

details.aspect: Leave spent on admin is not rest
details.description: Holiday entitlement used on appointments is holiday not taken, and the year ends with the leave gone and no break in it.
details.energy_note: Rested for none of the days you were off.

issues.title: Hold music, and the person who cannot help you
issues.category_name: Administrative burden: forms, queues, renewals, the time tax
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Support lines are built around cost per call. The person who answers can read the screen and rarely change what is on it.

details.description: Front-line staff work from a decision tree. Anything outside it needs an escalation to a team with no public number.
details.energy_note: Talking to someone who agrees with you and cannot act.

details.description: By the third person you are fluent in your own case and the organisation still has no memory of it.
A duplicate charge takes two calls, a webform, a chat session and eleven days. The money comes back. The four hours do not.
details.energy_note: Winning, at a loss.

details.description: A process that is tedious enough causes a predictable share of people to stop, which is cheaper than settling. Giving up is the designed outcome.
details.energy_note: Exhaustion, as a business model.

details.description: 'Someone will call you back within 48 hours' has no enforcement mechanism and no record you can point to.

issues.title: The typo that becomes official
issues.category_name: Errors: yours, theirs, and the ones nobody catches
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: One wrong character in a name, date, address or account number propagates into every system downstream, and correcting it is always harder than making it.

details.description: Later systems are populated from earlier ones, so the first version of your data becomes the authoritative one regardless of whether it was right.
details.energy_note: The earliest mistake wins.

details.aspect: Nobody can tell you where it started
details.description: By the time it surfaces, four organisations hold the same wrong value and each cites one of the others as the source.
details.energy_note: An error with no author.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the wrong digit in the date of birth
details.description: A clinic types 1987 instead of 1978. Eleven years later it surfaces as a mismatch on an insurance claim, and proving the original is wrong falls to the patient, who has no copy of a form filled in by someone else in 2014.
details.energy_note: Disproving a document you never saw.

details.description: Two digits swapped on a transfer. The money arrives in a real account belonging to a real stranger. Recovery depends on that stranger agreeing, and the bank will not identify them.
details.energy_note: Your money, in a named account, unreachable.

details.description: Change-of-detail requests trigger anti-fraud controls the original error never did, so the honest fix is scrutinised more than the mistake.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the address that never updated
details.description: One utility keeps the old address. Two years later a debt collector has a judgment for a bill posted to a house he left in 2021, and the first he hears is a refusal.
details.energy_note: Judged in absence, by post sent to the wrong door.

details.description: Mistyping your own email on a booking, your own IBAN on a form, your own postcode on an order. Same mechanism, same cost, and no one to escalate to.
details.energy_note: Nobody to be angry at.

issues.title: Their mistake, your problem
issues.category_name: Errors: yours, theirs, and the ones nobody catches
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.summary: Institutions presume their own records are correct. When they are not, discovering it, proving it and fixing it is entirely the work of the person harmed.

details.description: They have the record, the process and the lawyers. You have a memory of a phone call and a reference number that may not resolve.
details.energy_note: Arguing with an institution from memory.

details.aspect: You find out at the worst moment
details.description: Errors surface when they matter - at a border, a mortgage application, a hospital, a renewal - which is when you have least ability to stop and fix them.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the default that was not his
details.description: A default appears for a phone contract in a town he has never lived in. The dispute process takes thirty days. The mortgage offer expires in twenty-one.
details.energy_note: Right, and too late.

details.description: A correction is a correction. There is no mechanism to reimburse the forty hours and six weeks of anxiety it took to obtain.
details.energy_note: Restored, not repaid.

details.aspect: The correction is itself a flag
details.description: A file that changed is read by later reviewers as unstable, so being wronged leaves a small permanent mark.

issues.title: Mistaken for someone else
issues.category_name: Errors: yours, theirs, and the ones nobody catches
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.summary: Matching is fuzzy. A similar name, a shared birth date or a recycled phone number attaches another person's record - debts, fines, medical history - to you, and disproving it is your job.

details.description: Credit files, watchlists, medical records and collections all match on combinations that are not unique.

His new mobile number belonged to someone with unpaid accounts. He gets their collections calls for two years and cannot prove he is not them, because the caller will not say who they are looking for.
details.energy_note: Harassed on behalf of a stranger, indefinitely.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the allergy that was not his
details.description: A hospital merges his file with a same-name, same-birth-year patient. The chart lists an allergy he does not have and omits a medication he does take. He finds out because a nurse reads it back.
details.energy_note: A clinical near-miss produced by a coincidence.

details.description: Automated matching happens instantly. Separating two people takes human review at an organisation that has no process for it.

issues.title: After the crash
issues.category_name: Accidents and physical injury
issues.applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.scope_note: Anyone who drives or is driven. Includes crashes you caused.
issues.summary: The collision takes four seconds. What follows is months of insurers, assessors, hire cars, medical appointments and an argument about liability you did not want to have.

details.aspect: The claim is a second job
details.description: Photographs, statements, medical records, assessor appointments, adjuster calls, courtesy car arrangements - all handled by the person who is injured and has no car.
details.energy_note: Administered by whoever is least able to.

details.description: Both insurers act for their own client. A dispute over who was at fault can run for months while the repair waits.
details.energy_note: Your account of what happened, treated as a bid.

details.aspect: The premium goes up either way
details.description: A claim raises the renewal price whether or not the fault was yours, and the increase persists for years.
details.energy_note: Paying for years for four seconds.

details.description: Hit at 20 km/h at a junction. Barely any visible damage. Six weeks later the neck pain has not gone, physio is capped at eight sessions, and the other insurer has disputed liability.
details.energy_note: A minor accident that reorganises a year.

details.aspect: No car is its own problem
details.description: Until the repair or payout, getting to work, school and the shops becomes a daily logistics exercise with a cost attached.
He looked at his phone. Nobody was hurt. He still has the excess, the no-claims loss, the repair wait and the small private fact of having done it.
details.energy_note: The same paperwork, plus the part you cannot tell anyone.

issues.title: The ordinary injury
issues.category_name: Accidents and physical injury
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.summary: A fall, a ladder, a kitchen, a football pitch, ice. The healing is the easy part; the hard part is doing your job and your life at reduced capacity while nobody adjusts anything.

details.aspect: Sick leave is shorter than recovery
details.description: Statutory leave is measured in weeks; joints and soft tissue take months. The gap is absorbed privately.
details.energy_note: Back at work, not recovered.

details.description: Dressing, cooking, driving, typing, carrying shopping. The injury is not the pain, it is the four weeks of everything being slower.
details.energy_note: Not disabled. Just slower at all of it.

details.description: Six weeks in a cast, three months of physio, and he is right-handed. He works through it badly and nobody at work registers that the quarter was affected.
details.energy_note: Performing at 70% and appraised at 100%.

details.aspect: Physio is capped before you are better
details.description: Covered sessions run out at the point where progress is still being made, and continuing is a private purchase.

details.aspect: Some of it does not fully go
details.description: A minority of ordinary injuries leave a permanent limp, ache or weakness, and which ones is not predictable from the injury.
details.energy_note: Same accident, two outcomes, no explanation.

issues.title: You get ill, and nobody decided it
issues.category_name: Illness and injury that simply arrives
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.summary: Cancer, autoimmune disease, a cardiac event, a neurological condition. No behaviour reliably prevents them, no one is responsible, and the diagnosis reorganises everything around it.

details.aspect: The waiting is the first part of the illness
details.description: Symptom, GP, referral, waiting list, scan, waiting list, result. Months in which nothing is known and everything is suspected, before any treatment begins.
details.energy_note: Ill, untreated, and not yet allowed to be a patient.

details.aspect: It is not caused by anything you did
details.description: Most serious diagnoses come with no behavioural explanation available to the person receiving them, which removes the one form of control people reach for.
details.energy_note: No story to tell yourself about why.

details.aspect: Treatment is a job with a rota
details.description: Appointments, scans, infusions, bloods, reviews - scheduled by the hospital, not by you, across months, each one a day.
details.energy_note: A calendar written by someone else.

details.description: Three weeks between the scan and the result. She works, eats and sleeps badly through all of it. The result is benign. Nothing happened, and the three weeks are gone.
details.energy_note: Healthy, and it still cost a month.

details.description: A diagnosis draws a partner, parents and children into caring, worrying and rearranging. None of them chose it either.

details.aspect: Chronic means there is no after
details.description: For a condition managed rather than cured, there is no point at which the appointments, medication and monitoring stop.
details.energy_note: Not a crisis. A permanent second occupation.

issues.title: The waiting list
issues.category_name: Illness and injury that simply arrives
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Where care is rationed by queue rather than price, the wait is assigned to you without negotiation and without a date you can plan around.

details.aspect: No date, or a date that moves
details.description: A referral without a date cannot be planned around - work, childcare and travel all stay provisional for months.
details.energy_note: Unable to book anything, including your own life.

details.aspect: Deteriorating while you wait is normal
details.description: A joint, a cataract or a hernia gets worse on the list, so the wait itself changes the outcome and the recovery.

details.aspect: The private option is a price, not a choice
details.description: Going private is available to whoever can find the money, which converts a medical queue into a financial one.
details.energy_note: Rationed by queue, then rationed by price.

details.description: Therapy is offered after an eleven-week wait, capped at six sessions. It helps. It ends. The next referral restarts the eleven weeks.

issues.title: The illness generates an invoice
issues.category_name: Being billed for it: the health payment system you were born into
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: In systems that bill individuals, a medical event produces a bill nobody quoted in advance, for an amount nobody can state beforehand, from providers you did not choose.

details.description: Almost no other purchase requires agreeing before the cost is knowable. Treatment is agreed to first and priced afterwards.
details.energy_note: Signing for an amount nobody will state.

details.aspect: You did not choose the providers
details.description: The anaesthetist, the radiologist and the lab attached to your in-network hospital may each bill separately and may each be out of network.
details.energy_note: Billed by people you never met, at a hospital you did choose.

details.aspect: The bill arrives in pieces, for months
details.description: Facility, physician, imaging, pathology, follow-up - separate envelopes over half a year, so you never know when it is finished.
details.energy_note: No way to know whether it is over.

details.description: One night in hospital. Over the next five months: four bills from four entities, two of which he has to phone to understand, and one that turns out to duplicate another.

details.aspect: Prior authorisation is a delay with a clinical cost
details.description: A treatment the doctor has prescribed waits for an insurer's administrative decision, which takes weeks and can be refused.
details.energy_note: Your clinician overruled by an administrator.

details.aspect: Appealing a denial is unpaid work while ill
details.description: Denials are appealable, and the appeal is assembled by the patient - records, letters, calls - during the illness.

details.aspect: Being insured does not end it
details.description: Deductibles, coinsurance, caps and network rules mean a covered event still produces a substantial personal bill.
details.energy_note: Insured, and still paying for years.

details.description: In most systems dental and optical are separate, so a crown or a root canal becomes a clinical need decided on affordability.

issues.title: Cover attached to a job
issues.category_name: Being billed for it: the health payment system you were born into
issues.applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.scope_note: Anyone whose health cover runs through employment.
issues.summary: Where health cover comes through an employer, losing or changing work removes medical care at the same moment it removes income - and staying in a bad job becomes a medical decision.

details.description: The job ends and the cover ends. The gap is bridged at personal cost or not at all.
details.energy_note: Unemployed and uninsured on the same afternoon.

details.aspect: It removes the option of leaving
details.description: An employee with a chronic condition, a pregnancy or a dependent in treatment cannot weigh a job move purely on the job.
details.energy_note: Held in place by a medical need, not a contract.

details.description: The work is bad and the manager is worse. His daughter's medication is covered under the plan. He stays fourteen more months and stops mentioning it at home.

issues.title: The body slows on a timetable you do not set
issues.category_name: The body's own schedule
issues.imposed_by_note: The body and its schedule - ageing, injury, decline
issues.summary: Recovery lengthens, sleep degrades, eyesight goes, strength declines. Gradual enough to be invisible, cumulative enough to be decisive, entirely non-negotiable.

details.description: The injury that took two weeks at 25 takes eight at 45, and the effort that maintained fitness no longer does.
details.energy_note: The same life, costing more to run.

details.aspect: Reading glasses arrive for nearly everybody
details.description: Presbyopia is effectively universal from the mid-forties. A small, certain, scheduled loss that nobody plans for and everybody gets.
Waking at 3am, or not getting back to sleep, becomes routine - and there is nothing to report to a doctor.
details.energy_note: Tired in a way with no diagnosis.

details.description: He notices, at 47, that he thinks about the stairs before taking them. Not pain. Just a calculation that did not used to happen.
details.energy_note: The first time your body appears in a decision.

details.description: Teeth accumulate work over decades and each intervention makes the next more likely, at increasing cost.

issues.title: Being burgled or robbed
issues.category_name: Crime and other people's deliberate acts
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.summary: Someone decides to take your things. The loss is the smallest part; the aftermath is locksmiths, insurers, reference numbers, and not feeling right in your own rooms.

details.description: Electronics are insured. The ring, the photographs and the sense that the house is yours are not.
details.energy_note: Compensated for the cheap half.

details.aspect: Securing it again is immediate, and yours
details.description: Locks, a door, a window, a night somewhere else - arranged the same day by the person it happened to.

details.aspect: The claim wants proof you no longer have
details.description: Insurers ask for receipts and serial numbers for items stolen along with the box they came in.
details.energy_note: Asked to document what was taken, using what was taken.

details.description: A number, an email, and no further contact. Eleven months later the case is closed with no update, and he finds out by asking.
details.energy_note: Reported, recorded, and nothing.

details.description: Claiming for being a victim raises the price of being insured, and the claim must be declared at every future renewal.
details.energy_note: Charged extra for what was done to you.

details.aspect: The bike, the parcel, the phone
details.description: Smaller thefts are frequent enough to be routine and small enough that nothing happens - an ordinary tax on owning things, levied at random.

issues.title: On the receiving end of someone else's driving
issues.category_name: Crime and other people's deliberate acts
issues.applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.scope_note: Anyone on a road, including on foot or a bike.
issues.summary: Another person's speed, phone or inattention arrives in your life at a junction, and everything that follows is yours to administer.

details.aspect: Fault does not change your workload
details.description: Being blameless means the other insurer pays. It does not mean fewer calls, fewer appointments or a faster repair.
details.energy_note: Innocent, and doing all the paperwork.

details.aspect: Their insurer's job is to pay you less
details.description: The company assessing your injury is contractually aligned against your interest and is far more practised at this than you are.
A door opens. Broken collarbone, written-off bike, six weeks off. The driver was apologetic; their insurer disputes the value of the bike for four months.

issues.title: Where you live decides which disaster you get
issues.category_name: Weather, disaster and where you happen to live
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.summary: Flood, wildfire, hurricane, earthquake, heatwave, freeze. The exposure comes with the ground, and the ground came with the job, the family or the price.

details.description: The risk attaches to the location. Choosing a different one means moving away from work, family and everything already built.
details.energy_note: Priced into your address before you arrived.

details.aspect: Insurance withdraws where it is needed
details.description: In high-risk areas cover becomes expensive, restricted or unavailable - so exposure rises exactly where protection falls away.
details.energy_note: Uninsurable, in the place you already live.

details.aspect: Recovery is a year of administration
details.description: Assessors, contractors, quotes, permits, temporary accommodation - all run from a kitchen that no longer exists.
Water reaches six inches. Everything below it goes: floors, plaster, wiring, the bottom of every cupboard. The house looks fine from outside and is uninhabitable for nine months.

details.aspect: Heat and cold are now events
details.description: A week of extreme temperature turns housing, transport and work into a problem for anyone with no adaptation available to them.

details.aspect: The second time is harder to insure
details.description: A claim marks the property, so the next policy is dearer or narrower, and the value of the house follows.

issues.title: Someone is trying to defraud you, professionally
issues.category_name: Fraud, scams and identity theft
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.summary: Calls, texts, emails and messages engineered by people who do this full time, arriving whether or not you engage with anything.

details.aspect: It arrives whether you invite it or not
details.description: The contact is unsolicited. Not participating is not available; the only variable is how you respond.
details.energy_note: A stranger's business plan, aimed at you.

details.description: Your name, the last four digits, a recent transaction, your employer. Enough real context to sound legitimate, obtained from breaches you were never party to.
details.energy_note: Convincing, because the details are true.

details.description: Bank transfer and cryptocurrency have no chargeback, and those are exactly the methods the pressure steers you toward.
details.energy_note: Pushed onto the one road with no way back.

details.description: The number matched the one on the card. The caller knew the last transaction. She moved the money to a 'safe account' at 19:40 on a Thursday. The bank's position is that she authorised it.
details.energy_note: Not gullible. Targeted by a professional.

details.aspect: Proving you did not authorise it is your job
details.description: The dispute begins from the assumption that an authorised payment is authorised, and the evidence you would need is held by the bank.
Every unexpected call, link and message now requires a judgement. The tax is not the losses; it is never being able to answer the phone simply.
details.energy_note: Suspicion, as a permanent setting.

issues.title: Your data was lost by someone you never dealt with
issues.category_name: Fraud, scams and identity theft
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.summary: Organisations you have no relationship with hold records about you and lose them. Nothing you did caused it and nothing you can do fixes it.

details.description: Brokers, processors, clearing houses and subcontractors hold your details because a company you did use passed them on.
details.energy_note: Exposed by a firm whose name you had to look up.

details.description: The failure is theirs. Freezes, monitoring and new cards are all mitigation after the fact.
details.energy_note: Careful, and it made no difference.

details.description: Details taken now may not be used for years, by which point the free monitoring offered as compensation has expired.
details.energy_note: The apology runs out before the risk does.

details.description: New cards, new direct debits, new stored payment details across every subscription and account.

issues.title: The job ends because someone else did arithmetic
issues.category_name: Work, layoffs and career risk
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Layoffs, restructures, acquisitions and closures arrive on a timetable set elsewhere. The decision is about headcount and cost centres, not about you, and the income stops anyway.

details.aspect: Being good at it is close to irrelevant
details.description: Selection runs on role, cost centre and headcount target. Performance rarely determines whether the role exists next quarter.
details.energy_note: Losing something on grounds that have nothing to do with you.

details.aspect: The notice is short and the search is not
details.description: Severance is measured in weeks; a professional search is measured in months. The gap is the household's problem.
The meeting is at 9am and by 9:20 her laptop is locked. Eleven years of files she can no longer reach, including the only copies of things she wrote.
details.energy_note: Eleven years, ended before the coffee was finished.

details.aspect: The gap on the CV is read as a signal
details.description: Six months out is treated as information about the person rather than arithmetic about the market, and the longer it runs the more it reinforces itself.

details.aspect: Re-entry is usually at a discount
details.description: The next role commonly pays less, and every subsequent offer is benchmarked against the reduced figure.
details.energy_note: One quarter's decision, priced into the next twenty years.

issues.title: The manager you were assigned
issues.category_name: Work, layoffs and career risk
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.summary: Whether a job is tolerable is largely one person, allocated to you, who can change without notice and without any change to your contract.

details.description: You can accept a job partly because of a manager and have a different one within a year. Nothing you agreed to has changed.

details.aspect: The exit is the only real lever
details.description: Internal processes for a bad-but-lawful manager are weak everywhere. The options are endure, transfer or leave.
details.energy_note: Three options, two of which cost you the job.

details.description: He leaves after eighteen months. The manager he left is the reference the next employer will call. He lists a colleague instead and hopes nobody asks why.

issues.title: Working while ill, because the alternative is worse
issues.category_name: Work, layoffs and career risk
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Where sick pay is thin or absent, illness becomes a financial calculation, and the calculation usually says go in.

details.description: A day in bed costs a day's pay, so recovery is rationed against rent.
details.energy_note: Choosing between getting better and paying for March.

details.description: Working through it extends the recovery and spreads it to colleagues, which is a cost carried by everyone except the party that set the policy.
He goes in on day four still contagious because the fifth unpaid day is the one he cannot absorb.

issues.title: Your largest expense is set annually by someone else
issues.category_name: Housing, rent and the things that break
issues.applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: For renters, the price of having somewhere to live is decided by another party once a year, and the only counter-move costs more than accepting it.

details.description: The renewal is a notification, not a negotiation. The only leverage is a willingness to move.

details.aspect: Moving costs a multiple of the rise
details.description: Deposit, first month, agency fee, removals, time off, new utilities - and the old deposit is still held elsewhere.
details.energy_note: Priced out of leaving as well as staying.

details.description: Rent up 9%. The equivalent flat 11 miles out is 6% cheaper and adds 70 minutes of travel a day. She takes it, and buys back 3% of her income with 300 hours a year.
details.energy_note: Trading a third of a working month for 3%.

details.aspect: The deposit is your money and you cannot use it
details.description: The cash required to move is cash already sitting with a landlord.

details.aspect: You may be asked to leave for no reason
details.description: Where no-fault eviction exists, the household can be ended on notice with no cause stated and nothing to answer.
details.energy_note: Housed at someone else's pleasure.

issues.title: Things break, and they break together
issues.category_name: Housing, rent and the things that break
issues.applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.summary: Boiler, roof, car, washing machine, phone. Each has a lifespan, they were often bought at the same time, and they fail at whatever moment they fail at.

details.description: Appliances bought when you moved in fail within a few years of each other. The clustering is arithmetic, not bad luck.

details.aspect: Emergency pricing is the only pricing available
details.description: A failure that cannot wait is bought at the rate of whoever will come today and whatever part is in stock.
details.energy_note: The same repair, at the urgent price.

details.description: Boiler on the 6th, exhaust on the 14th, laptop on the 22nd. None is a catastrophe. Together they are the whole month.
Products are increasingly built so that the economic choice is replacement, which is a decision made by a manufacturer and paid for by you.

issues.title: Someone will need looking after
issues.category_name: Family, care and bereavement
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.summary: An ageing parent, a sick partner, a child with additional needs. It arrives unscheduled, lasts years, is unpaid, and lands on whoever is nearest or least able to refuse.

details.aspect: There is no end date to plan against
details.description: Care need generally escalates, and the only timeline is the one nobody wants to estimate.

details.aspect: Nobody assigns it and somebody does it
details.description: It falls to whoever lives closest, works most flexibly, or says no least easily. That is not a decision anyone made.
details.energy_note: Volunteered by geography.

details.aspect: The cost is earnings that never arrive
details.description: Reduced hours, declined promotions, early retirement, pension contributions foregone - invisible because it is income that never existed.
Every second weekend for four years. He does not take the job in another city. Nobody asks him to stay; he simply never applies.
details.energy_note: A decision made so gradually it never felt like one.

details.description: The end of caring is a bereavement and a sudden void of structure at once, usually after the carer's own networks have thinned.

issues.title: Bereavement, and the paperwork of it
issues.category_name: Family, care and bereavement
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.summary: Grief arrives with an administrative workload - registration, probate, accounts, utilities, pensions - executed by the person least able to concentrate.

details.aspect: Probate is slow and the costs are not
details.description: Estate administration commonly runs six to eighteen months, during which assets may be frozen while bills continue.

details.aspect: Every organisation must be told separately
details.description: Bank, utilities, pension, insurance, subscriptions, phone, memberships - each with its own process, each wanting a copy of the certificate, each asking you to say it again.
details.energy_note: Announcing the death forty times to forty strangers.

details.aspect: Funeral costs fall due before the estate opens
details.description: The expenses arrive before the money that would pay for them is accessible, so survivors pay from their own accounts.
Fourteen months later a charge appears in her father's name. Cancelling needs a password nobody has, and the retention script asks whether he would like to pause instead.
details.energy_note: Asked, by a chatbot, whether the dead would prefer to pause.

issues.title: Locked out of your own account
issues.category_name: Technology, data and digital dependency
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Identity online is a chain of recovery methods. Break one link - a dead number, a lost authenticator, a closed email - and the chain does not reconnect.

details.aspect: Recovery depends on something you may no longer control
details.description: Resets route to an email or phone. Losing the phone, changing the number or letting an old address lapse breaks everything downstream of it.
details.energy_note: A number you gave up in 2019 now holds your whole identity.

details.aspect: There is no human to appeal to
details.description: Consumer platforms at scale have no meaningful appeal path. The automated decision is the final decision.
details.energy_note: Adjudicated by a system with no counter.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the authenticator and the broken phone
details.description: The phone dies. The authenticator was not backed up. The recovery codes are in a password manager whose second factor is the authenticator. Nine accounts, including the bank and the tax portal, are now unreachable.
details.energy_note: A perfectly secure system, with you outside it.

details.description: Banking, tax, health records, work and government identity increasingly run through accounts. Opting out of the fragility means opting out of participating.

issues.title: The thing you relied on is discontinued
issues.category_name: Technology, data and digital dependency
issues.imposed_by_note: Another person's error, negligence, crime or decision, landing on you
issues.summary: Services close, formats are abandoned, apps are bought and shut, devices stop receiving updates. The decision is a company's; the migration is yours.

details.description: Notice is often weeks, and the export is usually into a format nothing else reads well.
A device that functions perfectly is retired by the end of security updates or a server being switched off.
details.energy_note: Forced to replace a thing that still works.

details.description: The external drive clicks. Recovery quotes start high with no guarantee. There is no second copy because there was never a moment when making one was urgent.
details.energy_note: The only irreplaceable things are the ones nobody insures.

details.description: Software you had learned is redesigned without consultation, and the relearning is unpaid.

issues.title: You must have a car, because of how the place was built
issues.category_name: Transport and getting places
issues.applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Where there is no viable transit, car ownership is not a preference - it is a condition of employment, imposed by planning decisions made before you arrived.

details.description: Purchase or finance, insurance, fuel, tax, servicing, tyres, parking - a standing annual cost for the ability to hold a job.
details.energy_note: A fee for being employable.

details.aspect: Losing the car loses the job
details.description: A breakdown, a write-off or a licence issue removes access to work in places with no alternative.
The quote is more than the car is worth. He cannot get to work without it and cannot afford to replace it, and both facts are true on the same Tuesday.

issues.title: The commute
issues.category_name: Transport and getting places
issues.applies_to_note: Only if you drive, rent, have children, and so on
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: A daily journey is the largest recurring involuntary time cost most working people carry. It is unpaid, not counted as work, and mostly set by where housing is affordable.

details.description: An hour each way, five days, forty-six weeks is about 460 hours - roughly eleven and a half working weeks a year, unpaid.
details.energy_note: Three months of working days, given away.

details.aspect: Housing and commute trade against each other
details.description: Cheaper housing is further out, so the rent saving is paid in hours - which means whoever has least money travels most.

details.aspect: Delays are not yours to fix
details.description: A cancelled train or a closed road is somebody else's failure, absorbed by you, with the lateness attributed to you.
details.energy_note: Blamed for a decision made by a signal box.

issues.title: The credential you must hold to be considered
issues.category_name: Credentials you must hold to be considered
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Employers set entry requirements. Roles that once needed a school certificate now need a degree, without a corresponding change in the work - so the qualification is a toll, not a choice.

details.aspect: The bar moves after you clear it
details.description: The requirement rises over a working life, so the credential that admitted you does not admit the next person, and may not readmit you.
details.energy_note: Qualified, then retrospectively underqualified.

details.aspect: You commit before you can evaluate
details.description: The decision is made at seventeen or eighteen, about a labour market fifteen years out, advised by people whose experience is a generation stale.
details.energy_note: A bet placed before you knew what betting was.

details.description: She retrains at 31 into a field that is hiring. By the time she qualifies at 34 the hiring has stopped. Nobody misled her; it was accurate when she acted.
Licensed fields require ongoing hours and fees to stay employable, paid by the worker and assumed by the employer.

issues.title: The structures that made friends are removed
issues.category_name: Social life, friendship and loneliness
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: School, university and early jobs supply repeated unplanned contact. Adult life does not, so friendship becomes something that must be organised or it ends.

details.aspect: Proximity did the work, and proximity goes
details.description: Nobody decides to stop being friends. One person moves and the thing that sustained it - being in the same place repeatedly - is simply absent.
details.energy_note: Nobody decided. It just stopped.

details.aspect: The organising falls to whoever minds most
details.description: Adult friendship runs on someone doing the scheduling, and that person eventually notices they are the only one doing it.

details.aspect: SCENARIO - the group chat that went quiet
details.description: Six people, fourteen years. Someone had a baby, someone moved, the messages thinned to birthdays. Nothing happened. It is simply over.

issues.title: You cannot afford to enforce your own rights
issues.category_name: Legal, contracts and disputes
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Most everyday legal wrongs are worth less than the cost of pursuing them, so the right exists and the remedy does not - and the other party knows it.

details.description: A modest dispute costs more to litigate than it is worth. Absorbing the loss is rational, and one party is relying on exactly that.
details.energy_note: A right you own and cannot use.

details.description: Consumer contracts routinely require arbitration and waive class actions, so the venue is chosen by the party you are complaining about.
The landlord withholds it for 'cleaning'. Adjudication takes eleven weeks and returns most of it. Appealing costs more than the difference.

details.aspect: Terms change and you agree by continuing
details.description: Contracts you rely on are amended unilaterally, with consent inferred from not cancelling a service you need.
details.energy_note: Agreement, assumed from your continued existence.

issues.title: Compelled participation
issues.category_name: Legal, contracts and disputes
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Jury service, tax filing, census, registration, court witness summons. Duties that take real time, are not optional, and are scheduled by the state.

details.aspect: The summons is not a request
details.description: Jury service is compulsory, of unpredictable length, and paid at a rate unrelated to what you earn.

details.aspect: Filing a return the authority could have calculated
details.description: In several countries the tax authority already holds the figures and still requires the individual to assemble, compute and submit them, or pay someone to.
details.energy_note: Homework set by an organisation that has the answers.

details.description: Called for two weeks. The trial runs eleven days. His employer pays the difference for five of them because that is the policy.

issues.title: Everything you have requires upkeep
issues.category_name: Maintenance, queues and entropy
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Possessions, accounts, documents, health and qualifications all decay without input. The work returns you to baseline; none of it is progress.

details.description: Servicing, renewals, cleaning, updates, check-ups, admin. Hours that prevent decline rather than produce anything.
details.energy_note: Running to stay level.

details.aspect: The load scales with what you have
details.description: A house, a car, children and a career each add a maintenance stream. Getting more means more things to keep working.
Professional knowledge has a half-life, and staying current is unpaid time that is nonetheless assumed.

issues.title: The queue
issues.category_name: Maintenance, queues and entropy
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Waiting is allocated to you by whoever is providing the thing, in units they do not pay for and you cannot spend elsewhere.

details.aspect: Your time is free to them
details.description: An organisation that shortens its queue pays for staff. An organisation that lengthens it pays nothing, because the cost lands on the person waiting.
details.energy_note: A cost with no invoice, borne entirely by you.

details.aspect: The queue has moved into your pocket
details.description: Waiting is now done at home, on hold, refreshing a portal, chasing a ticket - which looks like less queueing and is more.
Eleven minutes on hold, then a dropped call, then eleven minutes again, then the department closes at four.

issues.title: You were born into a cohort and the cohort has a price
issues.category_name: Luck, timing and the cohort you were born into
issues.imposed_by_note: Accident, illness, weather, timing - nobody decided it
issues.summary: House prices, interest rates, the labour market in your graduation year, whether a pandemic falls in your twenties. None is chosen, and all of it compounds.

details.aspect: Graduating into a downturn follows you
details.description: Entering the labour market in a bad year depresses earnings for many years afterwards, and is not fully recovered from.
details.energy_note: Penalised for the year you happened to turn 22.

details.description: Whether you bought before or after a price run-up will usually dominate every saving and career decision you ever make.
details.energy_note: Out-earned by a date.

details.aspect: And it is read as character
details.description: Cohort outcomes get described as generational virtue or generational failure, rather than as timing nobody selected.
details.energy_note: Congratulated or blamed for the decade you were born in.

issues.title: The volume of small compulsory decisions
issues.category_name: Psychological load and what it costs downstream
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: Tariffs, plans, policies, renewals and options all require comparison. The choosing is imposed; the alternative is paying the default price.

details.description: Deregulated markets replaced one price with forty, and the evaluation was transferred to the customer without compensation.
details.energy_note: Freedom, billed in hours.

details.description: Where comparison is too costly, people take the default - which is set by the seller and is rarely the best one.
details.energy_note: A fee for being busy.

details.description: Auto-renewal is a third more than the same cover bought fresh. He catches it in year one, forgets in year two, and pays the difference for four years.

issues.title: Ambient activation that never resolves
issues.category_name: Psychological load and what it costs downstream
issues.applies_to_note: Faced by most adults at some point
issues.imposed_by_note: The rules, institutions and markets you were born into and must comply with
issues.summary: News, notifications and always-on messaging produce a baseline of alertness nobody opted into, and it does not switch off because the devices do not.

details.description: Being contactable outside working hours was not agreed to; it arrived with the technology and then became the expectation.
details.energy_note: On call, without the allowance.

details.aspect: Sleep is the first thing spent
details.description: Sleep is sacrificed before anything else because it is the only resource with no immediate external consequence.
One work message, marked not urgent. He answers it, then lies awake composing the follow-up. Nobody asked him to; the notification was enough.
